boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Florida
boards.description: Ten Gainesville food destinations with currently documented late closing times or 24-hour availability.

cards.title: Bite of Power
cards.subtitle: 1412 W University Ave, Gainesville
cards.notes: Use the published address across from UF for a late pickup or meal; confirm the current listing before leaving if plans change.
cards.short_summary: Mediterranean-American food with a documented 3 a.m. closing time every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Bite of Power lists 1412 W University Ave, says it is across from the University of Florida, and publishes hours until 3 a.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Bite of Power
cards.access_notes: Published hours: Monday–Friday 11 a.m.–3 a.m.; Saturday–Sunday noon–3 a.m. The site advises checking its Google Business Profile for the most recent hours.

cards.title: Gumby's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 2028 SW 34th St, Gainesville
cards.notes: Order pickup when you need a food option after midnight; use the official ordering page to confirm availability for your night.
cards.short_summary: The Gainesville location publishes pickup service through 3 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Gumby's official Gainesville page lists its 2028 SW 34th Street address and pickup hours from 11 a.m. to 3 a.m. Monday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: Gumby's Pizza – Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Official published pickup hours are 11 a.m.–3 a.m. daily; delivery is listed through 2:30–2:45 a.m., depending on day.

cards.title: IHOP on SW 13th Street
cards.subtitle: 3625 SW 13th St, Gainesville
cards.notes: Choose this sit-down option when your schedule runs past normal dinner hours; check the location page before travel for service updates.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour Gainesville IHOP with dine-in, takeout, and delivery listed.
cards.evidence_claim: IHOP's official location page identifies 3625 SW 13th Street in Gainesville and lists the restaurant as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: IHOP Gainesville Late Night Food – 3625 SW 13th Street
cards.access_notes: The official page lists the restaurant as open 24 hours on every day of the week and identifies dine-in, takeout, and delivery amenities.

cards.title: Applebee's on NW 13th Street
cards.subtitle: 1005 NW 13th St, Gainesville
cards.notes: Plan a late dinner or takeout stop using the location’s posted day-by-day schedule, especially if you are heading out on a weekend.
cards.short_summary: A Gainesville restaurant with midnight weeknight and 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday hours listed.
cards.evidence_claim: Applebee's official Gainesville location page lists restaurant hours until midnight Sunday–Thursday and 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Applebee's Grill + Bar Restaurant in Gainesville, FL
cards.access_notes: Published restaurant hours: 11 a.m.–midnight Sunday–Thursday and 11 a.m.–1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Cantina Añejo
cards.subtitle: 1680 W University Ave, Suite 10, Gainesville
cards.notes: Use the posted day-specific closing times to plan a food-focused stop on University Avenue; reserve ahead only if your group needs it.
cards.short_summary: Mexican street-food restaurant with midnight-to-2 a.m. published closing times.
cards.evidence_claim: Cantina Añejo's official site lists its Gainesville address and hours until midnight Sunday–Tuesday and until 2 a.m. Wednesday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Cantina Añejo Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Published hours: Sunday noon–midnight; Monday–Tuesday 5 p.m.–midnight; Wednesday–Saturday closing at 2 a.m. Opening times vary by day.

cards.title: Spurrier's Gridiron Grille
cards.subtitle: 4860 Steve Spurrier Way, Gainesville
cards.notes: For a later Friday or Saturday meal, use the restaurant’s own schedule and confirm it before making the trip to Celebration Pointe.
cards.short_summary: Celebration Pointe restaurant with midnight Friday and Saturday hours published.
cards.evidence_claim: Spurrier's official menu page lists the Gainesville address and closing at midnight on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Spurrier's Gridiron Grille Menu
cards.access_notes: Published hours: Friday 4 p.m.–midnight and Saturday 11 a.m.–midnight; other listed days close at 10 p.m. or are closed Monday.

cards.title: Taco Bell on SW 13th Street
cards.subtitle: 1515 SW 13th St, Gainesville
cards.notes: Use the drive-through or dine-in schedule for a late food run, and check the official location page for any day-of changes.
cards.short_summary: This SW 13th Street Taco Bell lists drive-through service through 5 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell's official location page lists the 1515 SW 13th Street Gainesville restaurant, with drive-through hours until 5 a.m. and dine-in hours until 4 a.m. every day.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell Restaurant Near Me – 1515 SW 13th Street, Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Published daily hours: drive-through 8 a.m.–5 a.m.; dine-in 8 a.m.–4 a.m.

cards.title: V Pizza Gainesville
cards.subtitle: 115 SE 1st St, Gainesville
cards.notes: For a downtown meal after standard dinner hours, use the restaurant’s day-specific hours and order link before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Downtown pizza restaurant with published service through 2 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: V Pizza's official Gainesville page lists 115 SE 1st Street and hours until 2 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: V Pizza Gainesville Location
cards.access_notes: Published Friday–Saturday hours show 11 a.m.–midnight, with an additional 2 a.m. late-service time; other days list an additional midnight time.

cards.title: Checkers on W University Avenue
cards.subtitle: 912 W University Ave, Gainesville
cards.notes: Use pickup or the drive-through for a late meal near UF; check the location’s current order cutoff and posted daily hours first.
cards.short_summary: A University Avenue Checkers whose official page lists late-night service every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Checkers' official location page says the 912 W University Avenue restaurant is near the University of Florida and lists closing times of 3 a.m. or 5 a.m., depending on day.
cards.source_title: Checkers & Rally's – W University Ave, Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Published hours: 10:30 a.m.–3 a.m. Sunday–Tuesday and 10:30 a.m.–5 a.m. Wednesday–Saturday; online-order cutoff may be earlier.

cards.title: Waffle House #2387
cards.subtitle: 915 E University Ave, Gainesville
cards.notes: Use this East University Avenue diner when you need a round-the-clock meal; verify the store page before setting out during disruptions.
cards.short_summary: A named Gainesville Waffle House location listed by the company as open 24 hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House's official Gainesville location finder lists Waffle House #2387 at 915 E University Ave; the company’s individual location pages publish 24-hour daily operation for its locations.
cards.source_title: Waffle House Locations in Gainesville, FL
cards.access_notes: The official Gainesville finder identifies Waffle House #2387 at 915 E University Ave. Confirm its individual listing for the current 24-hour schedule before travel.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UF spaces for studying, gathering, recreation, and a quiet pause—each supported by a direct university, library, museum, or RecSports source.

cards.title: Plaza of the Americas
cards.subtitle: Historic campus green by Library West
cards.notes: Use the benches and lawn for an outdoor reset, then look for the historic live oaks that mark the Plaza’s 1931 dedication.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped historic green framed by UF’s early Collegiate Gothic campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Libraries documents the Plaza as a social space for studying, organization recruitment, special events, and conversation.
cards.source_title: The Plaza of the Americas: A Place for…
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; follow posted event and campus-use guidance.

cards.title: Reitz Union
cards.subtitle: 686 Museum Road
cards.notes: Meet a group in the union, then use its wayfinding map to locate the Game Room, Arts & Crafts Center, gallery, dining, or student services.
cards.short_summary: UF’s student union combines gathering areas, recreation, services, and event space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reitz Union describes itself as a space where students gather, collaborate, and exchange ideas, with recreation and student-service areas.
cards.source_title: Reitz Union
cards.access_notes: Individual areas, services, events, and reservations may have separate access rules or charges.

cards.title: Marston Science Library
cards.subtitle: 444 Newell Drive
cards.notes: Choose a collaboration floor for a group session or head to the fourth or fifth floor when you need a designated silent study area.
cards.short_summary: A science library with reservable rooms, technology lending, and distinct group and silent-study floors.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Libraries identifies Marston’s first through third floors for group study and its fourth and fifth floors for silent individual study.
cards.source_title: Study & Testing Spaces | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: Study-room reservations and library policies apply; check current library access information before visiting.

cards.title: Library West
cards.subtitle: 1545 West University Avenue
cards.notes: For focused work, use the fourth-floor quiet area; for collaboration, reserve a group room in advance rather than studying there solo.
cards.short_summary: The humanities and social-sciences library offers both quiet study and reservable group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Library West lists a fourth-floor quiet-study area and eighteen group study rooms intended for groups of two or more.
cards.source_title: Spaces | Library West
cards.access_notes: Group rooms require reservations; the graduate floor has Gator 1 access restrictions.

cards.title: Southwest Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 3150 Hull Road
cards.notes: Plan a movement break around the indoor track, courts, cardio areas, or social lounge, and check the facility’s current hours before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A large RecSports facility with fitness equipment, courts, track, activity rooms, and a social lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: UF RecSports lists strength and conditioning, basketball courts, cardio space, an indoor track, activity rooms, and a social lounge at SWRC.
cards.source_title: Southwest Recreation Center | RecSports
cards.access_notes: RecSports access and day-pass requirements apply; current weekday hours are listed as 5:30 a.m.–midnight.

cards.title: Student Recreation & Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: 244 Fletcher Drive
cards.notes: Use this central RecSports stop for basketball, volleyball, racquetball, squash, cycling, or a short strength-and-cardio session.
cards.short_summary: A central-campus recreation facility with courts, activity rooms, and fitness spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UF RecSports lists a multipurpose gym, strength room, activity rooms, cycle studio, cardio equipment, racquetball courts, and squash courts.
cards.source_title: Student Recreation & Fitness Center | RecSports
cards.access_notes: RecSports access and day-pass requirements apply; verify operating hours before visiting.

cards.title: Harn Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: UF Cultural Plaza
cards.notes: Walk the rotating galleries for an art-focused break, and consider Thursday’s extended Art After Dark hours when they fit your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus art museum with African, Asian, modern and contemporary art, photography, and changing exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harn states that admission to its exhibitions and programs is free and that its galleries feature rotating exhibitions and collection areas.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Harn Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; the museum posts current hours, including Thursday evening Art After Dark hours.

cards.title: Baughman Center
cards.subtitle: 982 Museum Road, beside Lake Alice
cards.notes: Visit on a weekday for a quiet indoor pause; do not enter when private-event signs are posted, and respect the site’s event and parking rules.
cards.short_summary: A lakeside contemplation space with prominent windows and natural materials.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Performing Arts says the Baughman Center is open to the public for private contemplation on weekdays and hosts private events at other times.
cards.source_title: Baughman Center | UF Performing Arts
cards.access_notes: Public contemplation hours: Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; Friday 8 a.m.–3 p.m.; closed weekends, holidays, and home football games.

cards.title: Lake Alice Field
cards.subtitle: South of Museum Road, across from Fraternity Row
cards.notes: Check the RecSports schedule or reservation status before heading over; the field is set aside for organized intramural, ROTC, and special-event use.
cards.short_summary: A named RecSports field within the Lake Alice area for organized campus activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UF RecSports states that Lake Alice Field is used by intramural sports and ROTC and may be reserved for special events.
cards.source_title: Lake Alice Field | RecSports
cards.access_notes: Not an open-recreation field; use depends on scheduled activities and reservations.

cards.title: Florida Pool
cards.subtitle: Outside the Student Recreation & Fitness Center
cards.notes: Bring proper swim attire and a valid Gator 1 card, then confirm weather and lifeguard hours before planning a lap-swim or recreation session.
cards.short_summary: An eight-lane, 50-yard outdoor pool beside the Student Recreation & Fitness Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UF RecSports identifies Florida Pool as an eight-lane, 50-yard outdoor pool and requires a valid Gator 1 Card for pool entry.
cards.source_title: Florida Pool | RecSports
cards.access_notes: Valid Gator 1 Card required; swimming is allowed only while a lifeguard is on duty and hours can change with weather.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-admission places around UF and Gainesville for an outdoor walk, wildlife viewing, art, or a quiet study hang.

cards.title: Study at Library West
cards.subtitle: 1545 W University Ave, UF campus
cards.notes: Meet during public visiting hours, choose an open seating area, and settle into a quiet conversation or shared study session.
cards.short_summary: Public visitors can study in Library West’s open seating areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Library West states that the general public may enter during scheduled visiting hours and study in its open seating areas; it also provides free onsite guest computing.
cards.source_title: Visitors | Library West
cards.access_notes: Open to the general public during scheduled visiting hours; after 10 p.m., entry requires an active UF or Santa Fe College ID.

cards.title: Watch the UF Bat Houses
cards.subtitle: Museum Road across from Lake Alice
cards.notes: Arrive before sunset, use the benches or viewing area, and watch quietly from behind the fence as the bats emerge.
cards.short_summary: A free, public dusk wildlife-viewing stop on the UF campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UF’s Florida Museum says visitors are welcome to observe the bats seven days a week and that there are no fees at the open-field site.
cards.source_title: Visit the Bat Houses
cards.access_notes: Observe from the designated area, remain behind the fence, and never handle bats. Emergence timing depends on weather.

cards.entity_name: Samuel P. Harn Museum of Art
cards.title: Browse the Harn Museum
cards.subtitle: Cultural Plaza, 3259 Hull Rd
cards.notes: Take a self-guided gallery lap, then pick one artwork each to discuss outside or in the museum’s public spaces.
cards.short_summary: A UF art museum with free admission for gallery visits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harn Museum of Art states that admission is free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Visit the Harn Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; check the museum’s visit page for current hours, closures, and gallery policies.

cards.title: Spread Out at Depot Park
cards.subtitle: 874 SE Fourth St, downtown Gainesville
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or use the promenade, then stroll the water’s edge or meet on the open lawn for conversation.
cards.short_summary: A City of Gainesville public park with paths, lawn, and conservation features.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Gainesville identifies Depot Park as a public city park with open green space, walking paths, picnic tables, and daily public access.
cards.source_title: Depot Park | City of Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor park; lit areas are listed as open 7 a.m.–11:30 p.m. Follow posted park rules.

cards.title: Walk Loblolly Woods
cards.subtitle: 3315 NW 5th Ave, Gainesville
cards.notes: Choose the shared path for an easy group walk, then pause at a picnic table before heading back toward campus.
cards.short_summary: A 159-acre City nature park along Hogtown Creek.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Gainesville lists Loblolly Woods Nature Park as a nature park with walking trails, picnic tables, and wildlife viewing, open daily from dawn to dusk.
cards.source_title: Loblolly Woods Nature Park | City of Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor nature park, dawn to dusk. Trails are shared with cyclists; keep to trails and follow city rules.

cards.title: Pause at Cofrin Nature Park
cards.subtitle: 4810 NW Eighth Ave, Gainesville
cards.notes: Walk the half-mile trail together, then use the shaded pavilion tables for a screen-free catch-up or a packed snack.
cards.short_summary: A City park with a short trail, picnic pavilion, and creekside woods.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Gainesville lists Cofrin Nature Park’s hiking trail, picnic tables, pavilion, and public daily hours.
cards.source_title: Cofrin Nature Park | City of Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor park. Hours are listed seasonally: 7 a.m.–8 p.m. March 15–September 30; 7 a.m.–6 p.m. otherwise.

cards.title: Follow Hogtown Creek at Ring Park
cards.subtitle: 1801 NW 23rd Blvd, Gainesville
cards.notes: Take the creekside trail at a relaxed pace, use the overlook as a regrouping point, and bring your own water.
cards.short_summary: A wooded City nature park with trails and a creek overlook.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Gainesville lists Alfred A. Ring Nature Park’s trails, picnic tables, wildlife viewing, and seasonal public hours.
cards.source_title: Alfred A. Ring Nature Park | City of Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor park. Parking is provided at the Elks Lodge at 2424 NW 23rd Boulevard; follow posted guidance.

cards.title: Take a Pedestrian Trail Break
cards.subtitle: 1502 NW 29th Rd, Gainesville
cards.notes: Meet on foot and take the shaded creekside trails slowly; this small park works well for a short daytime reset.
cards.short_summary: A pedestrian-access City nature park in the upper Hogtown Creek basin.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Gainesville lists 29th Road Nature Park’s nature trails, wildlife viewing, pedestrian-only access, and dawn-to-dusk hours.
cards.source_title: 29th Road Nature Park | City of Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor park, dawn to dusk. There is no parking available, so arrive by foot, bike, or transit nearby.

cards.title: Start at Boulware Springs
cards.subtitle: 3300 SE 15th St, Gainesville
cards.notes: Use the trailhead for a walk with friends, then regroup at the picnic tables near the historic springs setting.
cards.short_summary: A City nature park and trailhead for the Gainesville-Hawthorne State Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Gainesville identifies Boulware Springs Nature Park as a Gainesville-Hawthorne State Trail trailhead with public trails, picnic tables, and seasonal hours.
cards.source_title: Boulware Springs Nature Park | City of Gainesville
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor park. Hours are listed seasonally: 7 a.m.–8 p.m. March 15–September 30; 7 a.m.–6 p.m. otherwise.

cards.entity_name: Living History Farm at Morningside Nature Center
cards.title: Visit the Living History Farm
cards.subtitle: 3540 E University Ave, Gainesville
cards.notes: Visit Monday through Saturday, meet the farm animals, and take a slow look through the garden and historic farm setting.
cards.short_summary: A free City-operated living-history farm within Morningside Nature Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Gainesville’s seasonal guide identifies the Living History Farm at Morningside Nature Center as free and open Monday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Gainesville Parks, Recreation and Cultural Affairs Guide
cards.access_notes: Free; listed farm hours are 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Monday–Saturday. The farm is closed Sundays and certain holidays.

warnings: City nature-park pages document public access, amenities, and hours but may not enumerate a separate admission line. Parking or transportation can have separate costs; this board covers the hang itself.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented University of Florida library study environments, spanning quiet individual work, collaborative rooms, and specialized settings.

cards.title: Library West Quiet Study Floor
cards.subtitle: Library West, fourth floor
cards.notes: Bring quiet individual work to the fourth floor and keep devices non-audible; move calls and collaborative discussion to another library area.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet floor for individual study during Library West open hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Library West designates its fourth floor as quiet study, available first-come, first-served while the building is open.
cards.source_title: Quiet Study Floor | Library West | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served during Library West building open hours; group study is limited to designated group rooms.

cards.title: Library West Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Library West, reservable rooms
cards.notes: Reserve through LibCal with at least one other group member, save the confirmation, and use the room for collaborative work rather than solo study.
cards.short_summary: Reservable Library West rooms for groups of two or more.
cards.evidence_claim: Current UF students can reserve Library West group study rooms through LibCal for up to two hours per day, with two or more people required.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms | Library West | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: Current UF student reservation required; rooms are for group study of two or more, not individual study or proctored exams.

cards.title: Library West Graduate Study Floor
cards.subtitle: Library West, sixth floor
cards.notes: If you are an enrolled UF graduate student, use the sixth-floor individual-study area; confirm your access before heading upstairs.
cards.short_summary: A quiet individual-study floor restricted to enrolled UF graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Libraries identifies Library West's sixth floor as a quiet individual-study area reserved for enrolled UF graduate students.
cards.source_title: Study & Testing Spaces | George A. Smathers Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserved for enrolled UF graduate students; undergraduate and post-baccalaureate students taking graduate-level courses are excluded.

cards.title: Marston Science Library Collaboration Commons
cards.subtitle: Marston Science Library, first floor
cards.notes: Set up a group work session on the first floor, where the library places group-study rooms, computers, printing, and its collaboration commons.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor collaborative work setting with study rooms and technology nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: Marston's first floor includes more than 700 seats, 21 group study rooms, printing support, and the Collaboration Commons.
cards.source_title: Floorplans and Location | Marston Science Library | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use the first-floor collaboration setting for group work; individual room use is governed by Marston's study-room policy.

cards.entity_name: Marston Science Library Second-Floor Study Area
cards.title: Marston Science Library Second-Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: Marston Science Library, second floor
cards.notes: Choose this floor when you need group discussion alongside library services, course reserves, technology circulation, printing, and scanning.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor study area combining group work space with service and technology resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Marston's second floor provides group-study and discussion space along with a service desk, four group rooms, technology circulation, printing, and scanning.
cards.source_title: Floorplans and Location | Marston Science Library | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: A group-study and discussion area; consult the library's study-room policy before reserving a room.

cards.entity_name: Marston Science Library Third-Floor Study Area
cards.title: Marston Science Library Third-Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: Marston Science Library, third floor
cards.notes: Use the third floor for work that benefits from a discussion-friendly area near journals, theses, the aquarium, and data consultation resources.
cards.short_summary: A discussion-friendly Marston floor near research collections and data support.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Libraries lists Marston's third floor as a group-study and discussion area with journals, theses and dissertations, an aquarium, and a data consultation room.
cards.source_title: Floorplans and Location | Marston Science Library | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: Designed for group study and discussion; library building access and conduct rules apply.

cards.entity_name: Marston Science Library Fourth-Floor Quiet Study
cards.title: Marston Science Library Fourth-Floor Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: Marston Science Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Take individual reading or writing to the fourth floor, which the library identifies as quiet study and locates with its Books A–Z collection.
cards.short_summary: A quiet Marston floor for individual work amid the general book collection.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Libraries designates Marston's fourth floor as a quiet individual-study area; its floorplan lists Books A–Z and oversized books there.
cards.source_title: Floorplans and Location | Marston Science Library | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: Quiet individual-study area; follow Marston's library conduct expectations.

cards.entity_name: Marston Science Library Fifth-Floor Silent Study
cards.title: Marston Science Library Fifth-Floor Silent Study
cards.subtitle: Marston Science Library, fifth floor
cards.notes: For concentrated individual work, head to the fifth floor and keep the setting silent as the library designates for this level.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent individual-study area at the top of Marston Science Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Libraries identifies Marston's fifth floor as a silent individual-study area and the floorplan labels it for silent study.
cards.source_title: Floorplans and Location | Marston Science Library | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: Silent individual-study area; library building access and conduct rules apply.

cards.entity_name: Architecture & Fine Arts Library Reading Room
cards.title: Architecture & Fine Arts Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Architecture & Fine Arts Library, service floor
cards.notes: Use a powered carrel or larger table in the Reading Room, and keep extended group discussion elsewhere because sound carries in the open library.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading room with powered carrels, tables, and a sound-conscious atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The AFA Library Reading Room has double-decker carrels with electrical outlets and larger study tables; the library describes itself as a small, quiet open space.
cards.source_title: Study Space | Architecture & Fine Arts Library | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: Study space is available on both floors; extended group discussion is discouraged and food is not permitted.

cards.entity_name: Health Science Center Library Individual Study Rooms
cards.title: Health Science Center Library Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Health Science Center Library, reservable rooms
cards.notes: Book an individual room online in half-hour increments when you need a dedicated workspace, then retain the email confirmation for your reservation.
cards.short_summary: Reservable individual study rooms at the Health Science Center Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Health Science Center Library offers 18 individual study rooms for online reservations in half-hour increments, up to four hours per session.
cards.source_title: Health Science Center Library Study Spaces | UF Libraries LibCal
cards.access_notes: Online booking is available to current UF students and UF Health residents or fellows; reservations may run up to four hours per session.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named public-facing destinations on campus-adjacent Gainesville corridors, each with a documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Alachua County Library District Headquarters
cards.subtitle: East University Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the headquarters branch at 401 E. University Ave. when your route runs east from campus toward downtown and you need a public-library stop.
cards.short_summary: A named public-library destination on East University Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alachua County Library District identifies its Headquarters at 401 E. University Avenue in Gainesville.
cards.source_title: Alachua County Library District Long Range Plan
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current branch page for service and building hours.

cards.title: Matheson History Museum
cards.subtitle: East University Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Stop at 513 E. University Ave. for exhibits focused on Gainesville, Alachua County, and Florida history; confirm reopening information before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A downtown history museum with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum is located at 513 East University Avenue, presents local-history exhibitions, and lists free admission.
cards.source_title: Matheson History Museum: Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum’s visit page lists Wednesday–Saturday hours and notices temporary closures; check it before visiting.

cards.title: Bo Diddley Plaza
cards.subtitle: East University Avenue and Southeast First Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the covered-stage plaza as a downtown waypoint; the city documents it as a venue for concerts, festivals, gatherings, and picnic time.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown plaza built around a covered stage.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Gainesville describes Bo Diddley Plaza at Southeast First Street and East University Avenue as a venue for concerts, festivals, and gatherings.
cards.source_title: City of Gainesville: Cultural Facilities
cards.access_notes: Programming varies; consult the City of Gainesville events calendar for scheduled activities.

cards.title: Hippodrome State Theatre
cards.subtitle: Southeast Second Place corridor, beside Southwest First Avenue
cards.notes: Check the Hippodrome’s current ticket calendar when passing the downtown pedestrian-corridor area; its mainstage is at 25 SE 2nd Place.
cards.short_summary: A downtown theatre destination with scheduled ticketed performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hippodrome identifies its legal address as 25 SE 2nd Place, Gainesville, and its ticketing page lists mainstage performances there.
cards.source_title: The Hippodrome State Theatre: Planned Giving
cards.access_notes: Performance access and ticket availability vary by production; consult the theatre’s current schedule.

cards.title: Cade Museum for Creativity & Invention
cards.subtitle: South Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Head south on Main Street to the Cade at 811 S. Main St.; use its current visit page to choose an open day and obtain admission tickets.
cards.short_summary: A creativity-and-invention museum on South Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cade Museum lists its address as 811 South Main Street, Gainesville, and directs visitors to get tickets.
cards.source_title: Cade Museum for Creativity & Invention: Sitemap
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Thursday–Sunday opening, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; verify ticketing and any changes before arrival.

cards.title: Depot Park
cards.subtitle: Southeast Fourth Street corridor
cards.notes: Make Depot Park a destination along the southeast downtown route for its main pond and park setting; plan to leave before the city’s posted nightly closing time.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown park along the Southeast Fourth Street route.
cards.evidence_claim: A City of Gainesville communication states that Depot Park closes to the public each night at 11 p.m.
cards.source_title: City of Gainesville Commissioner Mail Archive: Depot Park closing information
cards.access_notes: The City states the park closes nightly at 11 p.m.; do not remain after closing.

cards.title: Cotton Club Museum & Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: Southeast Seventh Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Visit 837 SE 7th Ave. for exhibitions and programming centered on African-derived cultures, Gainesville history, and the African American music legacy.
cards.short_summary: A cultural institution in east downtown Gainesville.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cotton Club Museum & Cultural Center lists its location at 837 SE 7th Avenue and its mission includes preserving and sharing African American history and culture.
cards.source_title: Cotton Club Museum & Cultural Center: About Us
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Wednesday, Thursday, and Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; check its site for event-specific access.

cards.entity_name: A. Quinn Jones Museum & Cultural Center
cards.title: A. Quinn Jones Museum & Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: Northwest Seventh Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Follow Northwest Seventh Avenue to the former Jones family home for its permanent Prof Jones exhibit, neighborhood history, oral histories, and rotating displays.
cards.short_summary: A city museum documenting educator A. Quinn Jones and local history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says the museum at 1013 NW Seventh Avenue occupies the former Jones family home and presents exhibits and oral histories about Gainesville’s African American experience.
cards.source_title: City of Gainesville: A. Quinn Jones Museum & Cultural Center
cards.access_notes: The City lists Tuesday–Friday hours of 1–5 p.m., plus access by appointment and during special events.

cards.entity_name: The Historic Thomas Center Museum and Art Galleries
cards.title: The Historic Thomas Center Museum and Art Galleries
cards.subtitle: Northeast Sixth Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk Northeast Sixth Avenue to 302 NE Sixth Ave. to see the historic center, its art-gallery spaces, restored rooms, and gardens.
cards.short_summary: A city cultural center with galleries, historic spaces, and gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies the Historic Thomas Center at 302 NE Sixth Avenue and describes it as a cultural events center with contemporary art exhibitions and historical exhibits.
cards.source_title: City of Gainesville: Venues
cards.access_notes: Check the City’s Thomas Center page for gallery and event access before visiting.

cards.title: Rosa B. Williams Center
cards.subtitle: Northwest First Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the Rosa B. Williams Center at 524 NW First St. as a stop for participatory arts programming, including dance, music, gallery, and community art activities.
cards.short_summary: A named participatory-arts center near the Fifth Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes the Rosa B. Williams Center at 524 NW First Street as a participatory arts space with gallery and dance facilities.
cards.source_title: City of Gainesville: Venues
cards.access_notes: Classes and events vary; consult the City’s venue and events listings for current opportunities.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Florida rituals, songs, events and symbols that frame Gator gatherings.

cards.title: Make the Gator Chomp
cards.subtitle: UF game-day tradition
cards.notes: At a game or rally, place your right arm over your left and chomp along when the band plays the Jaws theme before kickoff.
cards.short_summary: A coordinated alligator-arm gesture used in Gator sports settings.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Student Life identifies the Gator Chomp as a Florida tradition, traditionally used before every kickoff with the Jaws theme.
cards.source_title: Chants & Cheers | Student Life Team
cards.access_notes: Follow event staff and venue guidance when attending athletics events.

cards.title: Stand Up for Mr. Two Bits
cards.subtitle: Pre-game cheer at UF home football
cards.notes: Listen for the pre-game call, then join the simple arm-circle motion and final raised arm if you are attending a home football game.
cards.short_summary: A pre-game call-and-response linked to longtime fan George Edmondson.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Student Life says the Mr. Two Bits Cheer is said before the start of each home football game.
cards.source_title: Chants & Cheers | Student Life Team
cards.access_notes: The cheer is part of home-football pre-game programming.

cards.title: Sway Through “We Are the Boys”
cards.subtitle: End-of-third-quarter football ritual
cards.notes: At the third-quarter break, stand with nearby fans, link shoulders when welcome, and sway left to right while singing the traditional song.
cards.short_summary: The stadium-wide third-quarter singalong and sway.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Student Life describes fans standing, putting arms around neighbors’ shoulders and singing while swaying after the third quarter of every home game.
cards.source_title: Chants & Cheers | Student Life Team
cards.access_notes: Participate only with consent and respect the space of people around you.

cards.title: Sing the Alma Mater After a Win
cards.subtitle: Football postgame song tradition
cards.notes: After a home win, stay through the final whistle and listen as the team, coaches, fans and band gather for the Alma Mater.
cards.short_summary: A post-win gathering around UF’s official school song.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Student Life states that the Alma Mater is performed at commencements and after home football wins with the team, coaches, fans and band.
cards.source_title: Chants & Cheers | Student Life Team
cards.access_notes: The post-win football performance depends on the game result.

cards.title: Learn “The Orange and Blue”
cards.subtitle: UF fight-song tradition
cards.notes: Use the official Student Life lyrics to follow the fight song at athletics events, rallies or other organized Gator gatherings.
cards.short_summary: UF’s fight song centers on cheering for the Orange and Blue.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Student Life publishes “The Fight Song” lyrics as part of its UF traditions chants-and-cheers guide.
cards.source_title: Chants & Cheers | Student Life Team
cards.access_notes: Follow the program cues at the event you attend.

cards.title: Answer “Orange” with “Blue”
cards.subtitle: Stadium call-and-response
cards.notes: At football or basketball, listen for the split-stadium chant: the east side calls “Orange” and the west side responds “Blue.”
cards.short_summary: A venue-wide Orange/Blue call-and-response used at Gator games.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Student Life says the east and west sides of the stadium trade “Orange” and “Blue,” most commonly during football and basketball games.
cards.source_title: Chants & Cheers | Student Life Team
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to athletics-event programming.

cards.title: See Gator Growl’s Homecoming Ritual
cards.subtitle: Student-led pep rally
cards.notes: Check UF Homecoming programming for the current edition of this student-led pep rally, historically scheduled before the Homecoming football game.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming pep rally introduced by Florida Blue Key in 1923.
cards.evidence_claim: UF News reports that Florida Blue Key added the student-run Gator Growl to Homecoming festivities in 1923 as a pep rally before kickoff.
cards.source_title: Gator Growl turns 100. Here's a look at the past 10 decades
cards.access_notes: Event format, location and admission can change; consult current Homecoming information.

cards.title: Watch the Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: Annual Homecoming-week procession
cards.notes: Look for the announced parade route during Homecoming Week and watch the student-organization floats from a lawful public viewing spot.
cards.short_summary: A themed float parade with roots in UF’s early Homecoming history.
cards.evidence_claim: UF News says the Fightin’ Gator Marching Band led the first Homecoming parade in 1916 and that student organizations later decorated floats.
cards.source_title: Gator Growl turns 100. Here's a look at the past 10 decades
cards.access_notes: Route, timing and viewing access are set annually by Homecoming organizers.

cards.title: Recognize the Gator Wrap
cards.subtitle: Student and alumni ring tradition
cards.notes: View the Alumni Association’s ring history and design before deciding whether this long-running student-and-alumni tradition is meaningful to you.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive UF ring tradition dating to the late 1930s.
cards.evidence_claim: The UF Alumni Association says the Gator Wrap has been a tradition among UF students and alumni since the late 1930s.
cards.source_title: Gator Wrap Ring
cards.access_notes: A ring is optional merchandise; consult the official program for current ordering details.

cards.title: Spot the Holiday Gator
cards.subtitle: Seasonal orange-and-blue campus installation
cards.notes: During the winter holiday season, check UF announcements before visiting the University Auditorium lawn to view the illuminated steel alligator.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal campus sculpture tradition that began in 2019.
cards.evidence_claim: UF News described the Holiday Gator as a new annual tradition: an orange-and-blue illuminated steel alligator near University Auditorium.
cards.source_title: Holiday Gator to return to UF
cards.access_notes: Seasonal display dates and installation status should be verified with current UF announcements.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Florida, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence that introduces UF’s campus landmarks, study spaces, art, recreation, and a recurring student program.

cards.title: Orient yourself with GatorWay
cards.subtitle: Self-guided campus tour · Start of the weekend
cards.notes: Download UF’s GatorWay app and use its self-guided tours to connect your first stops with the campus map.
cards.short_summary: Use UF’s own self-guided-tour tool to get your bearings before wandering farther.
cards.evidence_claim: UF’s visiting-campus page says self-guided tours are available through the GatorWay app and links visitors to the campus map.
cards.source_title: Visiting Campus | University of Florida
cards.access_notes: Bring a charged phone; app availability is through the App Store or Google Play according to UF.

cards.title: Pause at Plaza of the Americas
cards.subtitle: Historic campus green · After your map walk
cards.notes: Use the benches or picnic tables for a reset, then notice the historic buildings that frame this central green.
cards.short_summary: A campus green with seating and a documented history of student gathering and campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Libraries describes the Plaza as a student social and gathering space; UF’s 2017 renovation added lighting, benches, picnic tables, and greenery.
cards.source_title: The Plaza of the Americas: A Place for... | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public campus space; use normal campus-access rules.

cards.title: Look up at Century Tower
cards.subtitle: Historic core · Landmark stop
cards.notes: Walk to the tower beside University Auditorium and pause to hear the carillon if it is sounding during your visit.
cards.short_summary: A central UF monument with a cast-bell carillon and a World War memorial purpose.
cards.evidence_claim: UF identifies Century Tower as a heart-of-campus landmark commemorating the university’s 1853 founding and honoring students killed in World Wars I and II.
cards.source_title: Other Marks | University of Florida Brand Center
cards.access_notes: View from surrounding campus paths; tower interior access is not assumed.

cards.title: Make Library West your study landmark
cards.subtitle: 1545 West University Avenue · Midday reset
cards.notes: Browse the open seating areas or physical collections, and check the current visitor hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing library stop for studying, browsing collections, and getting familiar with a major campus resource.
cards.evidence_claim: Library West says onsite visitors may browse physical collections, scan materials, or study in open seating areas during scheduled visiting hours.
cards.source_title: Visitors | Library West | UF Libraries
cards.access_notes: General public entry is during scheduled visitor hours; after 10 p.m., active UF or Santa Fe College ID is required.

cards.title: Find the Alachua Sculpture
cards.subtitle: Near Marston Science Library · Campus-art detour
cards.notes: Take a photo-friendly walk past the large steel Alachua Sculpture before continuing toward the Reitz Union.
cards.short_summary: A named UF campus artwork also offered as a commemorative-card location by the university.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Business Services identifies the Alachua Sculpture, also called “French Fries,” as one of three memorable campus locations for its commemorative cards.
cards.source_title: Commemorative Cards | University of Florida Business Services
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork; follow nearby building and campus-access guidance.

cards.title: Get acquainted with the Reitz Union
cards.subtitle: 655 Reitz Union Drive · Afternoon hub
cards.notes: Walk through the student union to locate services and shared spaces you may use again during the semester.
cards.short_summary: UF’s student union gathers services, programs, dining, study areas, and recreational spaces in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: UF’s catalog identifies the Reitz Union as the student union and lists its Game Room, Arts & Crafts Center, study spaces, meeting rooms, lounges, and student services.
cards.source_title: Student Life | University of Florida Undergraduate Catalog
cards.access_notes: Building hours for fall/spring 2026 are listed as ending at 11 p.m.; hours are subject to change.

cards.entity_name: Samuel P. Harn Museum of Art
cards.title: Spend an hour at the Harn
cards.subtitle: UF Cultural Plaza · Art stop
cards.notes: Choose a gallery or exhibition to explore, then check the museum’s visit page for same-day hours and closures.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission campus art museum with rotating exhibitions and collections in several art areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harn says it is on the UF campus, admission is free, and its art on view includes traveling exhibitions plus African, Asian, modern and contemporary art, and photography.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Harn Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s current hours and closure notices before visiting; donations are accepted but not required.

cards.title: Plan a Lake Wauburg outing
cards.subtitle: RecSports destination · Daytime recreation
cards.notes: Arrange a daytime visit with friends, confirm entry rules, and decide whether you want general access or a boating pass.
cards.short_summary: A UF RecSports lake destination with distinct entry and boating-access options.
cards.evidence_claim: RecSports states that Lake Wauburg entry-day-pass holders have general access to North Shore and field-equipment checkout, while boating passes are separate.
cards.source_title: Visit Lake Wauburg | UF RecSports
cards.access_notes: UF students, faculty/staff, and RecSports members are listed at $0 for entry; boating access requires a separate pass. Guests need a GatorOne-holder sponsor.

cards.title: Watch for the bat emergence
cards.subtitle: 2664 Museum Road · Evening wildlife stop
cards.notes: Arrive before evening emergence, stay on the visitor area, and observe quietly without approaching or disturbing the bats.
cards.short_summary: A campus wildlife-viewing stop where visitors are welcome to watch bats emerge in the evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: UF says the bat houses and signage are at Field & Fork Farm and Gardens on Museum Road across from Lake Alice, and visitors may observe evening emergence seven days a week.
cards.source_title: UF Bat Houses | University of Florida
cards.access_notes: Observe from the designated visitor area; UF notes bats may swoop for insects and advises visitors not to provoke them.

cards.title: Check the GatorNights calendar
cards.subtitle: Recurring UF student program · Weekend close
cards.notes: Look up the current program, confirm its location, and bring your student status details for event check-in if you attend.
cards.short_summary: A documented recurring UF student program with changing activities and locations.
cards.evidence_claim: UF Student Engagement says GatorNights is for currently enrolled UF students, has operated since August 25, 2000, and posts current event information online.
cards.source_title: GatorNights | UF Student Engagement
cards.access_notes: Attendance is limited to currently enrolled UF students; check the live calendar because program dates and locations vary.
